chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: Reunion at Small's Paradise and Savoy Sundays
summary: She met him again outside Small's Paradise in 1935-36; he invited her to the Savoy where he played with Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: No, no, I ran into him here in New York. Lucy and I were on our way to the Lafayette Theatre, Edgar Hayes's wife. We were turning into 135th Street, Small's Paradise there. He was standing out there -
'35, '36, something like that. He was standing in front of Small's Paradise. Lucy and I passed and I said,
"That looks like a fellow I met him in Charleston, Jay C. Higginbotham," and she said, "Come, on, come on, let's go." He followed us; he walked behind us.

Yeah, and when we got to the Lafayette Theatre he walked up and said, "Aren't you Margaret Bryant?" I said, "No, I'm Margaret Stratton," because I'd married. But he knew me as Margaret Bryant. He said, "When you come out of the theatre, come over to the Savoy Ballroom. I'm playing over there in Chick Webb's band." So we did. So that was our Sunday routine; we'd go to the Lafayette Theatre and look at the show and then we'd go over to the Savoy Ballroom. Everybody did.
About '36, '37. That's when Lana Turner and all that gang used to -
Oh, yeah. I sat at the next table to her. at Small's Paradise. She and her three body guards.
